# quotapool

> A Go library that limits calls to third-party API providers whose quotas are
> shared across processes and come in different shapes. Its defining feature is
> atomic batch admission: a request for N permits reserves all N or none.

quotapool models two independent dimensions per resource — concurrency (a
distributed semaphore with leases) and rate (a sliding window) — and evaluates
both in a single atomic step. It targets the case where several service replicas
share one provider account, so a process-local limiter cannot see the quota the
rest of the fleet is consuming.

Import path: github.com/laconhub/quotapool
License: Apache-2.0
Go: 1.25+

## Core API

- `New(store Store, opts ...Option) *Limiter` — construct a limiter.
- `(*Limiter).Acquire(ctx, resource string, n int) (Release, error)` — reserve n permits atomically, blocking up to the wait budget.
- `(*Limiter).TryAcquire(ctx, resource string, n int) (Release, error)` — single non-blocking attempt.
- `(*Limiter).SetQuota(resource string, q Quota) error` — change limits at runtime.
- `(*Limiter).Quota(resource string) (Quota, bool)` — read current limits.
- `(*Limiter).Stats() Stats` — admission counters.
- `Release` — func() returned by Acquire; idempotent, safe from any goroutine.

## Types

- `Quota{Concurrency int, Rate int, Window time.Duration}` — zero on a dimension means unconstrained; zero value means unlimited.
- `Store` — two methods, `Acquire(ctx, AcquireRequest) (bool, error)` and `Release(ctx, resource, tokens) error`. Acquire must be atomic across all constrained dimensions.
- `AcquireRequest{Resource, Quota, Tokens, LeaseTTL, Now}` — one all-or-nothing admission attempt.
- `Stats{Admitted, Rejected, FailedOpen, FailedClosed, Released, ReleaseFailed uint64}`.

## Stores

- `NewRedisStore(client RedisClient, opts ...RedisStoreOption) *RedisStore` — shared across processes. `RedisClient` is satisfied by go-redis Client, ClusterClient, Ring and UniversalClient. `WithKeyPrefix(string)` namespaces keys.
- `NewMemoryStore() *MemoryStore` — single process; same semantics, no sharing.

## Options

`WithQuotas(map[string]Quota)`, `WithMaxWait(d)` (default 8s), `WithLeaseTTL(d)`
(default 30s), `WithBackoff(min, max)` (default 40ms/250ms),
`WithReleaseTimeout(d)` (default 3s), `WithFailClosed()`, `WithLogger(*slog.Logger)`,
`WithNowFunc(func() time.Time)`.

## Errors

`ErrQuotaExceeded`, `ErrBatchTooLarge`, `ErrInvalidCount`, `ErrInvalidQuota`.
Reported only under `WithFailClosed()`; the default policy admits and logs instead.

## Behavioural notes for code generation

- The default failure policy is fail-open: on store error, wait-budget expiry, or an impossible batch, Acquire returns a usable Release and a nil error. Use `WithFailClosed()` when over-admission is worse than blocking.
- An unregistered resource is unlimited and never reaches the store.
- Concurrency permits are leased and reclaimed on expiry; rate permits are never released, they age out of the window.
- `Release` is idempotent; calling it twice is safe. It runs on its own timeout, so it still works after the request context is cancelled.
- A batch larger than a configured dimension resolves immediately rather than consuming the wait budget.
- `Limiter` is safe for concurrent use.
